General Institute Requirements

Synthetic policy summary: not less than three regular academic terms; include the term of graduation; departmental permission; only by petition. Transfer students generally will graduate under the requirements that apply to the class they join. minimum of 48 units of unrestricted electives; does not include ROTC subjects; a GIR CI-M will not be included in the "units beyond" calculation.

Synthetic credit conditions: lose it if they take 18.01; 3 units of elective credit if they take 18.01A. No Physics II without having first received credit for a Physics I. Advanced credit substitution: 6 units of elective credit in place of 8.01.

Synthetic milestones: two CI subjects in the humanities; two CI subjects in their major. one of their CI subjects by the end of the first year; two by the end of the second year; three by the end of the third year; four by graduation. Only one CI-H subject per term. Placement exemptions include score of 5 on either relevant AP test, or score of 7 on the English A or B Higher-Level exam. All other students must take writing-focused instruction as their first CI subject. Normally, these students will take four CI-M subjects for double majors; exceptions can be common to both departments.

Synthetic HASS plan: minimum of eight subjects. Three of the eight subjects cover humanities, arts, and social sciences. Concentrations require either three or four subjects. Proposal in second term of junior year; One of the subjects may overlap with permission of the concentration advisor. Completion form in final term prior to graduation. A special concentration may be arranged with advance approval. The remainder of the eight-subject requirement uses any distribution category or subjects designated as HASS electives.

Synthetic REST policy: two subjects from the list below; no more than one in their department; exception for subjects designated with a J.

Synthetic lab policy: 12 units in sum designated as lab credit. Subject units beyond the 12 needed are counted as units beyond the GIRs.

Synthetic PE options: Transfer students need to complete four points (two courses). Swimming may use passing the swim test. Four points are awarded for varsity participation; ROTC has a maximum of four points. Complete by the end of their second year or submit a plan for a time extension.
